previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, prior cerebrovascular accidents with aphasia and contractures, dysphagia, and chronic constipation was admitted for lethargy and found to be in septic shock. Initial evaluation revealed MRSA pneumonia and Clostridioides difficile infection as sources. He was intubated for airway protection but extubated the following day as his mental status returned to baseline. He required vasopressor support briefly, which was discontinued as hemodynamics stabilized. Acute kidney injury secondary to hypotension resolved with fluid resuscitation. Antibiotics were narrowed to vancomycin for both MRSA and C. diff. His bowel regimen was adjusted, and psychiatric medications were changed to improve safety. He was discharged to extended care on continued IV and oral vancomycin, with stable vital signs, improved mentation, and tolerance of enteral feeds.

HISTORY:  Congestion and fever.

FINDINGS:  The study is significantly limited by multiple factors, mainly due
to positioning.  The patient's chin overlies the lung apices.  The patient is
significantly rotated.  There are low lung volumes with hazy opacity above
both diaphragms, presumably atelectasis.  No definite consolidation or
superimposed edema is noted.  There is marked aortic tortuosity.  Cardiac
silhouette size is difficult to assess but grossly is likely enlarged, of
indeterminate chronicity.  No left effusion is noted.  There is blunting of
the right costophrenic angle suggesting a small effusion.  No pneumothorax is
seen.  Please note the patient has a tracheostomy and apparently there is an
oxygen face mask over it.  There is marked levo-concave curvature of the
thoracic spine, likely due to positioning.  Multilevel degenerative change is
noted.  The bones are diffusely osteopenic.

superimposed infection identified, although poor evaluation of the lung bases
and extreme lung apices as above.
